library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Centanni_2026_vincristine"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Centanni_2026_vincristine"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.70303> (open access)

Centanni et al. pooled the vincristine concentrations and CTCAE neuropathy
grades of 35 Dutch children (the bolus-versus-infusion trial of van de Velde
et al. 2020) and 15 Kenyan children (the CHAPATI feasibility study) and
re-estimated the PK and PK-neuropathy models of Centanni et al. 2024 (see
`Centanni_2024_vincristine`). The question was why Kenyan children tolerate
higher vincristine doses with little vincristine-induced peripheral
neuropathy (VIPN), and how two kinds of selection bias distort a model
extrapolated from Dutch to Kenyan children: informative censoring (Type I)
and population differences in effect modifiers (Type II).

The packaged model is the final model of Table 2, estimated on the pooled
data:

* **PK.** Three compartments: linear elimination from the central
  compartment, linear distribution to a peripheral compartment, and
  saturable uptake into a binding compartment,
  `Bmax x A_central / (Kb + A_central)`, with first-order return `kp`.
  CL, Vc, Q and Vp scale allometrically to 70 kg (exponents 0.75 and 1,
  fixed). One shared coefficient lowers CL and Vp in Kenyan children,
  `exp(-0.786 x Kenyan)` (Equation 4). Infusions start after a lag time;
  the residual error is additive on log concentrations, larger for infusion
  samples, with IIV on the infusion residual.
* **Neuropathy.** A proportional-odds model with a Markov element for each of
  four CTCAE subscores (peripheral sensory and motor neuropathy,
  constipation, neuralgia) on three levels (0, 1, >= 2):
  `logit P(>= 1) = B1|0 + Emax x AUC / (AUC50 + AUC) + B1|0,Grade>0 x [previous grade > 0]`
  and `logit P(>= 2) = logit P(>= 1) + B2|0`. `Emax` and `B2|0` differ
  between neuralgia/motor and constipation/sensory. `AUC = dose / CL` of the
  current occasion. In Kenyan children `Emax = exp(-100 x 20)`, effectively
  zero.
* **Censoring.** A separate logistic model (Equation 2) for the probability
  that an assessment is censored: a baseline logit with step increases from
  the first, second and third dosing occasions, and an increase after a
  previous grade >= 2 in any subscore. The VIPN probabilities are scaled by
  `1 - P(censored)` so the four categories sum to 1 (Equation 3).

The model outputs the cumulative VIPN probabilities `p_vipn_ge1_nm`,
`p_vipn_ge2_nm` (neuralgia and motor) and `p_vipn_ge1_cs`, `p_vipn_ge2_cs`
(constipation and sensory), not yet scaled for censoring, and the censoring
probabilities `p_cens_vipn` (no previous grade >= 2) and `p_cens_prev_vipn`
(a previous grade >= 2 in any subscore). The Markov state of a subscore
enters through `PREV_AE_SCORE`, the dosing occasion through `CYCLE` and the
Kenyan cohort through `REGION_KENYA`.

The paper's structure is taken from its published NONMEM code (Supporting
Information S2), and the values from Table 2.

# Population

The Dutch cohort comprised 35 children aged 2-17 years (64% with acute
lymphoblastic leukemia, ALL), randomized to an IV bolus (20) or an infusion
(15; 60 min standard, of which 38 min vincristine and 22 min flushing).
They received 1.5 or 2 mg/m^2 (cap 2 mg) on one to five occasions and were
sampled at 10, 20, 30, 40, 60, 75 and 140 min and at 24 h when still
hospitalised. The Kenyan cohort comprised 15 children aged 5-14 years
(ALL, Hodgkin lymphoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, neuroblastoma, nephroblastoma)
given 2 mg/m^2 (cap 2.5 mg) as a bolus, sampled at 60, 90 and 240 min on two
occasions. The analysis used 513 plasma concentrations and 800 neuropathy
assessments from 50 children (Methods; Supporting Methods S1). The article
reports no demographic table beyond the age ranges.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Centanni_2026_vincristine")()$population`.

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each
`ini()` entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Centanni_2026_vincristine.R`.
The table below collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` | log(42.2) L/h at 70 kg | Table 2 CL |
| `lvc` | log(14.5) L | Table 2 Vc |
| `lq` | log(71.6) L/h | Table 2 Q |
| `lvp` | log(541.5) L | Table 2 Vp |
| `e_region_kenya_cl_vp` | -0.786 (shared on CL and Vp) | Table 2; Equation 4; S2 `THETA(7)` |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.75, 1 (fixed), 70 kg | Methods 'Pharmacokinetic Model'; Table 2 footnote a |
| `ltlag` | log(0.02) h, fixed (infusions only) | S2 `THETA(6)` 0.02 FIX; Table 2 prints 2 min |
| `lvmax_bind` | log(7.17) mg/h | Table 2 Bmax |
| `lkm_bind` | log(5.03) ug | Table 2 Kb |
| `lk31` | log(28.3) 1/h | Table 2 kp |
| `etalcl` | 0.77705 (108.4%) | Table 2 IIV CL |
| `etalvc` | 1.16386 (148.4%) | Table 2 IIV Vc |
| `etaltlag` | 0.419665 (72.2%), fixed | Table 2 IIV LAG; S2 `$OMEGA` ETA(3) |
| `etaRUV` | 0.46846 (77.3%) | Table 2 IIV RUVprop, infusion |
| `expSd_bolus`, `expSd_infusion` | 0.36, 0.38 | Table 2 RUV (log scale, footnote c) |
| `b1_vipn` | -10, fixed | Table 2 B1\|0 |
| `b_prev_vipn` | 2.989 | Table 2 B1\|0, if Grade > 0 |
| `b2b1_nm_vipn`, `b2b1_cs_vipn` | -1.102, -3.583 | Table 2 B2\|0 |
| `emax_nm_vipn`, `emax_cs_vipn` | 8.697, 9.149 | Table 2 Emax |
| `e_region_kenya_emax_vipn` | 20, fixed | Table 2 Kenyan Emax parameter |
| `auc50_vipn` | 2.587 ng\*h/mL | Table 2 AUC50 |
| `b_cens_vipn` | -144.7 | Table 2 PX0 B3 \| Baseline |
| `b_cens_occ1_vipn`, `_occ2_`, `_occ3_` | 136.9, 5.764, 1.502 | Table 2 Censoring \| OCC > 0, > 1, > 2 |
| `b_cens_prev_vipn` | 3.05 | Table 2 Censoring \| Grade > 0; S2 applies it when a previous subscore is > 1 |
| Three-compartment ODEs with saturable binding | -- | Results 'Pharmacokinetic Model'; S2 `$DES` |
| Allometry and Kenyan effect | -- | Equation 4; S2 `$PK` |
| VIPN logits, Markov term, Kenyan Emax | -- | Results 'Pharmacodynamic Model'; S2 `$PRED` |
| Censoring logit and outcome scaling | -- | Equations 2-3; S2 `$PRED` |
| Omega from CV% | `log(1 + CV^2)` | Table 2 footnote b |

# Pharmacokinetics: typical profiles

```{r typical-pk}
mod <- readModelDb("Centanni_2026_vincristine")

# The typical-value solves below remove all random effects, so rxode2 reports
# that the model has no sigma and that several subjects are simulated without
# omega. Those two warnings, and only those, are expected here.
muffle_typical <- function(w) {
  if (grepl("No sigma parameters|multi-subject simulation without",
            conditionMessage(w))) {
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
}
mod_typ <- withCallingHandlers(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), warning = muffle_typical)

pk_times <- c(0, 0.017, 0.033, 0.05, 0.083, 0.117, 0.167, 0.25, 0.333, 0.5,
              0.667, 0.75, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2, 2.33, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 36,
              48, 72, 96, 120, 144, 168)

typ_cases <- tibble::tibble(
  id = 1:3,
  case = c("Dutch, 1.5 mg bolus", "Dutch, 1.5 mg over 1 h",
           "Kenyan, 1.5 mg bolus"),
  TINF = c(0, 1, 0),
  REGION_KENYA = c(0, 0, 1)
)
typ_ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(typ_cases, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = 1.5,
                rate = ifelse(TINF > 0, -2, 0)),
  tidyr::expand_grid(typ_cases, time = pk_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cmt = "central", WT = 30, CYCLE = 1, PREV_AE_SCORE = 0) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

typ_sim <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = typ_ev, keep = "case",
                  returnType = "data.frame"),
  warning = muffle_typical
)

ggplot(dplyr::filter(typ_sim, time <= 24), aes(time, Cc, colour = case)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after start of dose (h)", y = "Vincristine (ng/mL)",
       colour = NULL,
       title = "Typical-value profiles for a 30 kg child")
```

Kb = 5.03 ug corresponds to about 0.35 ng/mL in the central compartment of
a 70 kg patient (Discussion), below the early concentrations, so uptake
into the binding compartment runs close to `Bmax` right after the dose and
stays above half of it for the first day:

```{r kb-check}
kb_conc <- 5.03 / 14.5
bolus_typ <- dplyr::filter(typ_sim, id == 1) |>
  dplyr::mutate(frac_bmax = central / (5.03e-3 + central))
stopifnot(
  abs(kb_conc - 0.35) < 0.01,
  all(bolus_typ$frac_bmax[bolus_typ$time > 0 & bolus_typ$time <= 0.25] > 0.9),
  all(bolus_typ$frac_bmax[bolus_typ$time <= 16] > 0.5)
)
bolus_typ |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(0.083, 0.25, 1, 4, 24)) |>
  dplyr::select(time, Cc, frac_bmax) |>
  dplyr::rename("Time (h)" = time, "Cc (ng/mL)" = Cc,
                "Uptake rate / Bmax" = frac_bmax) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

Because all elimination leaves the central compartment linearly and the
binding compartment returns everything it takes up, the area under the
concentration curve of a single dose is `dose / CL` despite the saturable
step. The paper's exposure metric for the neuropathy model rests on that
identity. The trapezoidal AUC of the typical profiles confirms it:

```{r auc-identity}
auc_check <- typ_sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(id, case) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    auc_trap = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2),
    auc_dose_cl = 1.5 / cl[1] * 1000,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = auc_trap / auc_dose_cl)
stopifnot(all(abs(auc_check$ratio - 1) < 0.03))
auc_check |>
  dplyr::rename("Case" = case, "Trapezoidal AUC0-168 (ng*h/mL)" = auc_trap,
                "Dose / CL (ng*h/mL)" = auc_dose_cl, "Ratio" = ratio) |>
  dplyr::select(-id) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

# Virtual cohort and simulation scenarios

The paper simulated 100,000 children per scenario with age drawn from the
age-specific incidence of ALL (1-18 years), weight and height from CDC growth
references for Dutch children and adjusted Kenyan growth charts, and BSA by
DuBois (Methods). Those growth inputs are not reported. The cohort below is
a stand-in built by the maintainers: ages 1-18 years weighted towards the
ALL peak at 2-5 years, weight and height from approximate CDC median
growth curves with log-normal scatter (weight CV 15%, height CV 4%,
correlation 0.7), and the same cohort used for every scenario. Absolute
exposures therefore differ from Table 3; the comparisons that do not depend
on the cohort (ratios between scenarios, censoring) are the validation.

```{r cohort}
n_per_arm <- 200

growth <- tibble::tibble(
  age = c(1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18),
  wt = c(10, 12.5, 16.3, 20.5, 25.6, 32.5, 41, 51, 59, 64),
  ht = c(76, 87, 103, 116, 128, 139, 151, 163, 170, 173)
)
age_weights <- c(0.04, rep(0.11, 4), rep(0.06, 4), rep(0.025, 9))
age_weights <- age_weights / sum(age_weights)

set.seed(2026)
cohort <- tibble::tibble(id = seq_len(n_per_arm)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    age = sample(1:18, n_per_arm, replace = TRUE, prob = age_weights) +
      stats::runif(n_per_arm),
    z_wt = stats::rnorm(n_per_arm),
    z_ht = 0.7 * z_wt + sqrt(1 - 0.7^2) * stats::rnorm(n_per_arm),
    WT = stats::approx(growth$age, growth$wt, xout = pmin(age, 18))$y *
      exp(0.15 * z_wt),
    HT = stats::approx(growth$age, growth$ht, xout = pmin(age, 18))$y *
      exp(0.04 * z_ht),
    BSA = 0.007184 * WT^0.425 * HT^0.725
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(id, age, WT, HT, BSA)

summary(dplyr::select(cohort, age, WT, BSA))
```

Table 1 of the paper defines five scenarios. Scenarios 0-3 use models
estimated on the Dutch data alone (Supporting Information Tables S2 and S3),
which have no Kenyan covariate effects; Scenario 4 is the packaged pooled
model. Scenario 3 adds two literature corrections: a CYP3A5 mixture on CL
(1.87-fold CL in the 90% of Kenyan children who are high expressers) and an
intercept shift of -0.52 (ABCB1 rs4728709) - 0.19 (CEP72 rs924607) = -0.71
on the VIPN logits.

```{r scenario-models}
omega_cv <- function(cv) log(1 + cv^2)

# Table S2: Dutch data, no censoring (PK identical in Table S3)
mod_s2 <- rxode2::ini(
  mod,
  lcl = log(39.99), lvc = log(13.17), lq = log(70.18), lvp = log(555.7),
  lvmax_bind = log(7.5), lk31 = log(28.5), lkm_bind = log(5.56),
  e_region_kenya_cl_vp = 0,
  etalcl ~ 1.04906, etalvc ~ 1.82504,
  b2b1_nm_vipn = -1.101, emax_nm_vipn = 8.688, emax_cs_vipn = 9.138,
  auc50_vipn = 2.541
)
# Table S3: Dutch data with censoring (Bmax printed in ug/h, 7504 = 7.504 mg/h)
mod_s3 <- rxode2::ini(
  mod,
  lcl = log(39.99), lvc = log(13.17), lq = log(70.18), lvp = log(555.7),
  lvmax_bind = log(7.504), lk31 = log(28.47), lkm_bind = log(5.561),
  e_region_kenya_cl_vp = 0,
  etalcl ~ 1.04906, etalvc ~ 1.82504
)
mod_s3_high <- rxode2::ini(mod_s3, lcl = log(39.99 * 1.87), b1_vipn = -10.71)
mod_s3_low <- rxode2::ini(mod_s3, b1_vipn = -10.71)

stopifnot(
  abs(omega_cv(1.362) - 1.04906) < 1e-4,
  abs(omega_cv(2.281) - 1.82504) < 1e-4
)
```

Each scenario gives one dose to every child (1.5 mg/m^2, cap 2 mg, in the
Dutch Scenario 0; 2 mg/m^2, cap 2.5 mg, in the Kenyan scenarios), observes
the plasma profile for 168 h, and then evaluates the neuropathy and
censoring probabilities at occasions 1-5 for a previous subscore grade of 0
and of > 0. The dose and CL do not change between occasions in the paper's
simulation (Table 3 shows constant AUC in Scenarios 0 and 1), so one dose
fixes the occasion AUC.

```{r scenario-events}
prob_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(CYCLE = 1:5, PREV_AE_SCORE = 0:1) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 200 + seq_len(dplyr::n()))

make_events <- function(cohort, mg_per_m2, cap_mg, kenya) {
  doses <- cohort |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = pmin(mg_per_m2 * BSA, cap_mg), time = 0, evid = 1L,
                  CYCLE = 1, PREV_AE_SCORE = 0)
  pk_obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(dplyr::select(cohort, id, WT), time = pk_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, CYCLE = 1, PREV_AE_SCORE = 0)
  pd_obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(dplyr::select(cohort, id, WT), prob_rows) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0)
  dplyr::bind_rows(dplyr::select(doses, id, WT, time, evid, amt, CYCLE,
                                 PREV_AE_SCORE),
                   pk_obs, pd_obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(cmt = "central", rate = 0, TINF = 0, REGION_KENYA = kenya) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

ev_dutch <- make_events(cohort, 1.5, 2, kenya = 0)
ev_kenya <- make_events(cohort, 2, 2.5, kenya = 0)
ev_kenya_pooled <- make_events(cohort, 2, 2.5, kenya = 1)

n_high <- round(0.9 * n_per_arm)
high_ids <- cohort$id[seq_len(n_high)]

run_scenario <- function(model, events, seed) {
  rxode2::rxSetSeed(seed)
  rxode2::rxSolve(model, events = events, returnType = "data.frame")
}

sims <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  run_scenario(mod_s2, ev_dutch, 101) |> dplyr::mutate(scenario = "0"),
  run_scenario(mod_s2, ev_kenya, 102) |> dplyr::mutate(scenario = "1"),
  run_scenario(mod_s3, ev_kenya, 102) |> dplyr::mutate(scenario = "2"),
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    run_scenario(mod_s3_high, dplyr::filter(ev_kenya, id %in% high_ids), 104),
    run_scenario(mod_s3_low, dplyr::filter(ev_kenya, !id %in% high_ids), 105)
  ) |> dplyr::mutate(scenario = "3"),
  run_scenario(mod, ev_kenya_pooled, 106) |> dplyr::mutate(scenario = "4")
)
stopifnot(!anyNA(sims$Cc))
```

# Exposure: PKNCA and Table 3

```{r pknca}
# Children with a high CL reach integrator noise (a tiny negative undershoot)
# within 168 h: assert the undershoot is noise, floor it, and drop the
# numerically-zero tail so the half-life fit does not follow it.
pk_part <- dplyr::filter(sims, time <= 168, !is.na(Cc))
stopifnot(all(pk_part$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(pk_part$Cc)))
conc <- pk_part |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(scenario, id) |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= time[which.max(Cc)] | Cc >= 1e-6 * max(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, id, time, Cc)
dose_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::select(ev_dutch, id, time, evid, amt), scenario = "0"),
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::select(ev_kenya, id, time, evid, amt),
                scenario = list(c("1", "2", "3"))) |>
    tidyr::unnest(scenario),
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::select(ev_kenya_pooled, id, time, evid, amt),
                scenario = "4")
) |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, id, time, amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | scenario + id,
                             concu = "ng/mL", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | scenario + id,
                             doseu = "mg", route = "intravascular")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE,
                        aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj,
                                          intervals = intervals))

per_subject <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, id, aucinf = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    sims |>
      dplyr::filter(time == 0) |>
      dplyr::distinct(scenario, id, cl, auc_occ),
    by = c("scenario", "id")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = aucinf / auc_occ)

# PKNCA AUC0-inf against the closed-form dose / CL used by the neuropathy model
stopifnot(
  abs(median(per_subject$ratio) - 1) < 0.03,
  quantile(abs(per_subject$ratio - 1), 0.9) < 0.08
)
summary(per_subject$ratio)
```

Table 3 reports the mean AUC and CL of each scenario. Occasion 1 is
compared below; later occasions differ only by who remains uncensored.

```{r table3}
sim_means <- per_subject |>
  dplyr::group_by(scenario) |>
  dplyr::summarise(aucinf.obs = mean(aucinf), cl = mean(cl), .groups = "drop")

published_t3 <- tibble::tibble(
  scenario = c("0", "1", "2", "3", "4"),
  aucinf.obs = c(110.47, 154.75, 155.59, 90.38, 330.26),
  cl = c(30.22, 25.52, 25.30, 45.61, 11.32)
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = dplyr::select(sim_means, scenario, aucinf.obs),
  reference = dplyr::select(published_t3, scenario, aucinf.obs),
  by = "scenario",
  units = c(aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
cmp |>
  dplyr::rename("Scenario" = scenario) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Mean AUC at occasion 1, simulated (maintainers' cohort, 200 children)",
    "versus Table 3. * differs by more than 20%."
  ), digits = 1)

dplyr::left_join(sim_means, published_t3, by = "scenario",
                 suffix = c("_sim", "_paper")) |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, cl_sim, cl_paper) |>
  dplyr::rename("Scenario" = scenario, "Mean CL, simulated (L/h)" = cl_sim,
                "Mean CL, Table 3 (L/h)" = cl_paper) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

The absolute means depend on the stand-in cohort and, with a 136% CV on CL
in Scenarios 0-3, carry a sampling error of roughly 10% at 200 children;
the Scenario 3 row is the one outside 20%. The cohort cancels out of the
ratios between scenarios that share it. Using
the expected mean `E[CL] = CL_typ x exp(omega^2 / 2)` over the cohort's
weights:

```{r cl-ratios}
wt_term <- mean((cohort$WT / 70)^0.75)
mean_cl <- c(
  s2 = 39.99 * exp(1.04906 / 2) * wt_term,
  s3 = 39.99 * (0.9 * 1.87 + 0.1) * exp(1.04906 / 2) * wt_term,
  s4 = 42.2 * exp(-0.786) * exp(0.77705 / 2) * wt_term
)
ratios <- tibble::tibble(
  Comparison = c("Scenario 4 / Scenario 1", "Scenario 3 / Scenario 2"),
  `Expected from the model` = c(mean_cl[["s4"]] / mean_cl[["s2"]],
                                mean_cl[["s3"]] / mean_cl[["s2"]]),
  `Table 3, occasion 1` = c(11.32 / 25.52, 45.61 / 25.30)
)
stopifnot(all(abs(ratios[[2]] / ratios[[3]] - 1) < 0.1))
knitr::kable(ratios, digits = 3)
```

The pooled model's lower Kenyan CL (Scenario 4) and the CYP3A5 mixture's
higher CL (Scenario 3) are both reproduced to within 6%.

```{r figure3, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3 of Centanni 2026 at occasion 1 (AUC per child; maintainers' cohort)."}
ggplot(per_subject, aes(scenario, aucinf)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, fill = "mistyrose") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(80, 100), linetype = 2) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 200)) +
  labs(x = "Scenario", y = "AUC (ng*h/mL)")
```

# Censoring: patients remaining per occasion

Figures 3 and 4 print the number of the 100,000 simulated children still
under observation at each occasion. In Scenario 4 the Kenyan Emax is
effectively zero, no child reaches grade >= 2, and the retention is set by
the censoring model alone. Each child has four subscore assessments per
occasion and is lost once any of them is censored, so the expected number
remaining after occasion `k` is
`100,000 x prod_{j <= k} (1 - Pc_j)^4`:

```{r retention}
pc <- sims |>
  dplyr::filter(scenario == "4", time > 200, PREV_AE_SCORE == 0) |>
  dplyr::distinct(CYCLE, p_cens_vipn) |>
  dplyr::arrange(CYCLE)
stopifnot(nrow(pc) == 5)
retention <- tibble::tibble(
  Occasion = 1:5,
  `P(censored), one subscore` = pc$p_cens_vipn,
  `Expected n remaining` = 1e5 * cumprod((1 - pc$p_cens_vipn)^4),
  `Figure 3/4 n, Scenario 4` = c(100000, 61120, 9621, 1534, 241)
)
stopifnot(all(abs(retention[[3]] / retention[[4]] - 1) < 0.02))
knitr::kable(retention, digits = c(0, 4, 0, 0))
```

The expected numbers agree with the printed ones to within the sampling
error of a 100,000-child simulation. This pins the occasion coding
(`CYCLE = 1` for the assessment after the first dose, so the first dose
occasion sees only the `OCC > 0` step) and the per-subscore censoring.

# Neuropathy over occasions: Figure 4

The Markov simulation below follows the paper's scheme: at each occasion,
each of the four subscores of a child draws grade 0, 1, >= 2 or censored
from Equation 3, given its own previous grade; the censoring probability
uses the higher value when any subscore was >= 2 at the previous
assessment; a child with a censored subscore leaves the simulation.
Scenarios 0 and 1 use models without censoring. Each of the 200 simulated
children is followed through 50 independent outcome histories.

```{r markov-functions}
prob_table <- function(sims, scen) {
  sims |>
    dplyr::filter(scenario == scen, time > 200) |>
    dplyr::select(id, CYCLE, PREV_AE_SCORE, p_vipn_ge1_nm, p_vipn_ge2_nm,
                  p_vipn_ge1_cs, p_vipn_ge2_cs, p_cens_vipn, p_cens_prev_vipn)
}

simulate_vipn <- function(probs, n_rep, censoring, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  ids <- sort(unique(probs$id))
  n <- length(ids) * n_rep
  row_id <- rep(seq_along(ids), times = n_rep)
  grade <- matrix(0, n, 4) # columns: constipation, sensory, motor, neuralgia
  active <- rep(TRUE, n)
  any_ge2_prev <- rep(FALSE, n)
  out <- vector("list", 5)
  for (occ in 1:5) {
    p_occ <- dplyr::filter(probs, CYCLE == occ) |> dplyr::arrange(PREV_AE_SCORE, id)
    p0 <- dplyr::filter(p_occ, PREV_AE_SCORE == 0)[row_id, ]
    p1 <- dplyr::filter(p_occ, PREV_AE_SCORE == 1)[row_id, ]
    pc <- if (censoring) ifelse(any_ge2_prev, p0$p_cens_prev_vipn, p0$p_cens_vipn) else 0
    censored <- rep(FALSE, n)
    new_grade <- grade
    for (k in 1:4) {
      grp <- if (k <= 2) "cs" else "nm"
      prev_pos <- grade[, k] > 0
      ge1 <- ifelse(prev_pos, p1[[paste0("p_vipn_ge1_", grp)]], p0[[paste0("p_vipn_ge1_", grp)]])
      ge2 <- ifelse(prev_pos, p1[[paste0("p_vipn_ge2_", grp)]], p0[[paste0("p_vipn_ge2_", grp)]])
      u <- stats::runif(n)
      censored <- censored | u < pc
      v <- (u - pc) / (1 - pc)
      new_grade[, k] <- ifelse(v < ge2, 2, ifelse(v < ge1, 1, 0))
    }
    active <- active & !censored
    grade <- new_grade
    any_ge2_prev <- apply(grade >= 2, 1, any)
    out[[occ]] <- tibble::tibble(
      occasion = occ,
      n_fraction = mean(active),
      pct_ge2 = 100 * mean(any_ge2_prev[active])
    )
  }
  dplyr::bind_rows(out)
}
```

```{r markov-run}
n_rep <- 50
vipn <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  simulate_vipn(prob_table(sims, "0"), n_rep, censoring = FALSE, seed = 201) |>
    dplyr::mutate(scenario = "0"),
  simulate_vipn(prob_table(sims, "1"), n_rep, censoring = FALSE, seed = 202) |>
    dplyr::mutate(scenario = "1"),
  simulate_vipn(prob_table(sims, "2"), n_rep, censoring = TRUE, seed = 203) |>
    dplyr::mutate(scenario = "2"),
  simulate_vipn(prob_table(sims, "3"), n_rep, censoring = TRUE, seed = 204) |>
    dplyr::mutate(scenario = "3"),
  simulate_vipn(prob_table(sims, "4"), n_rep, censoring = TRUE, seed = 205) |>
    dplyr::mutate(scenario = "4")
)

published_f4 <- tibble::tibble(
  scenario = rep(c("0", "1", "2", "3", "4"), each = 5),
  occasion = rep(1:5, 5),
  pct_paper = c(2.7, 11.1, 16.1, 19.0, 20.9,
                2.9, 12.5, 18.2, 21.4, 23.4,
                2.9, 12.3, 16.4, 19.0, 15.9,
                1.2, 3.4, 4.3, 5.5, 2.9,
                0.001, 0, 0, 0, 0),
  n_paper = c(rep(100000, 10),
              100000, 59161, 8178, 1113, 170,
              100000, 60467, 9411, 1431, 206,
              100000, 61120, 9621, 1534, 241)
)

vipn_cmp <- dplyr::left_join(vipn, published_f4, by = c("scenario", "occasion")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(n_sim = 1e5 * n_fraction)

# Scenario 4: Kenyan Emax is effectively zero, so grade >= 2 is (almost) absent
stopifnot(max(vipn_cmp$pct_ge2[vipn_cmp$scenario == "4"]) < 0.5)

vipn_cmp |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, occasion, pct_ge2, pct_paper, n_sim, n_paper) |>
  dplyr::rename("Scenario" = scenario, "Occasion" = occasion,
                "Grade >= 2, simulated (%)" = pct_ge2,
                "Grade >= 2, Figure 4 text (%)" = pct_paper,
                "n remaining per 100,000, simulated" = n_sim,
                "n remaining, Figure 4" = n_paper) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 0, 1, 3, 0, 0))
```

```{r figure4, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4 of Centanni 2026: proportion of children still observed with grade >= 2 VIPN (any subscore) per occasion. Points: values reported in the Results text."}
ggplot(vipn_cmp, aes(occasion, pct_ge2)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#b5476b", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(aes(y = pct_paper), shape = 21, fill = "white", size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~scenario, labeller = label_both) +
  labs(x = "Dose occasion", y = "Grade >= 2 VIPN (%)")
```

**The neuropathy incidence of Figure 4 is not reproduced.** With the Table 2
(and Table S2/S3) estimates, AUC50 = 2.6 ng\*h/mL lies far below the
occasion AUCs of 30-300 ng\*h/mL, so the drug effect is saturated at
`Emax` for nearly every child, the grade >= 1 logit of a neuralgia or motor
subscore at occasion 1 is about -10 + 8.7 = -1.3, and roughly 12-15% of
children are predicted to reach grade >= 2 in at least one subscore after
the first dose. The paper reports 2.7-2.9% in Scenarios 0-2, rising to
about 21% by occasion 5. The packaged model's Scenario 0-3 percentages are
several-fold higher at every occasion and do not match the published
trajectory; the maintainers found no reading of the printed parameters or
the published code that yields both the occasion-1 value and the later rise
without changing an estimate, and did not tune any. The parts of Figure 4
that the model does reproduce are the qualitative ordering of the scenarios
(Scenario 3 below Scenario 2, Scenario 4 essentially zero) and the
censoring-driven retention. The retention of Scenarios 2 and 3 is lower
than published because more simulated children reach grade >= 2, which
raises their censoring probability.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Model code over the printed table.** The structure follows the NONMEM
  code of Supporting Information S2. Where the code and Table 2 disagree,
  the code is used: the infusion lag time is fixed at 0.02 h (1.2 min;
  Table 2 prints 2 min), and the censoring shift `Censoring | Grade > 0`
  applies when any subscore was above grade 1 at the previous assessment
  (`PDV.GT.1`; the Table 2 label and the Results text say grade > 0). The
  second reading is supported by Figure 3/4: the 3% shortfall of Scenario 2
  against Scenario 4 at occasion 2 (59,161 vs 61,120) matches the 2.9% of
  children with grade >= 2 at occasion 1, not the larger fraction with
  grade >= 1. The code otherwise lists initial estimates; all values come
  from Table 2.
* **Exposure metric.** The paper names the occasion AUC as the exposure
  driving neuropathy, as in Centanni 2024, where it is defined as
  `dose / CL`; the same definition is used here. The published code
  reads the exposure from a placeholder (`BM = A(1)`) that does not define
  it.
* **Figure 4 not reproduced.** See the section above. The VIPN parameters
  are transcribed as printed (Table 2, which equals Table S3 except for the
  Kenyan Emax, and Table S2).
* **Units.** Bmax is printed in Table 2 as 7.17 'mg'; it is a rate (mg/h)
  in the code's differential equations, where it appears in ug/h (Table S3
  prints 7504). Kb is an amount in ug and is converted to mg in the model,
  whose amounts are in mg.
* **Unused code terms.** The PK code carries an IIV term on an unused
  quantity (`PBP`, THETA(8) = 0 FIX) and the neuropathy code a drug effect
  on censoring fixed at 0 (THETA(9)) and an IIV fixed at 0; none affects the
  model and none is included.
* **Covariates.** `REGION_KENYA` is the paper's nationality indicator (0 =
  Dutch, 1 = Kenyan); nationality, enrollment country and study coincide.
  Censoring after a grade >= 2 in any subscore spans the four subscore
  chains, so it is returned as two outputs (`p_cens_vipn`,
  `p_cens_prev_vipn`) rather than read from a covariate. Platelet count was
  tested on CL and binding and not retained.
* **Infusions.** `TINF` sets the infusion duration (the code's `D1 = INFT`)
  and marks infusion samples for the lag time and the infusion residual
  error. The paper does not say whether INFT was the 60-min total or the
  38-min vincristine time; the Kenyan doses were all boluses.
* **Scenario models.** Tables S2 and S3 list no lag time or residual-error
  terms; the packaged values are kept for those, which affect neither AUC
  nor the neuropathy model. Tables S2 and S3 also list IIV on Q (54.2%),
  which the packaged model has no term for; Q does not change `dose / CL`.
  For Scenario 3 the CYP3A5 mixture multiplies the Table S3 CL by 1.87 in
  90% of children, which reproduces the Table 3 CL ratio of Scenario 3 to
  Scenario 2, and the -0.71 intercept shift is applied to `B1|0`, shifting
  both VIPN logits.
* **Virtual cohort.** The maintainers' stand-in cohort (above) replaces the
  paper's age-incidence and growth-chart sampling, one cohort is used for
  Dutch and Kenyan scenarios, and 200 children per scenario replace
  100,000; each dose is a bolus and doses do not change between occasions.
* **Load-time note.** rxode2 reports "some etas defaulted to non-mu
  referenced" for `etaRUV` whenever the model is parsed: the IIV on the
  infusion residual error multiplies the residual SD rather than sitting in
  a mu-referenced parameter. It affects estimation efficiency, not
  simulation (the same note appears for `Centanni_2024_vincristine`).
* **Not reproduced.** Figure 2 (the VPC of the observed neuropathy grades)
  needs the observed data. Figures S1-S4 are diagnostics of the fit.
